{{dsp|example-random-id-jThf}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-jThf}}
{{judri|c10e16d4}}
:'''le nanmu cu batci le gerku .i zu'a le verba cu cadzu le bisli'''
:<code>The man bites the dog. [Left] the child [something] walks-on the ice.</code>
:''The man bites the dog. To the left of the child, something walks on the ice.''

Here the first place of the second sentence is unspecified, because {{vla|zu'a}} has absorbed the sumti 
:{{jbo|le verba}}.

Do not confuse either {{lex|example-random-id-9Q0x}} or {{lex|example-random-id-jThf}} with the following:

{{ind|general-imported|separately tensed sentences|contrasted with tense connected sentences}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense connected sentences|contrasted with separately tensed sentences}}

{{dsp|example-random-id-MzxF}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-MzxF}}
{{judri|c10e16d5}}
:'''le nanmu cu batci le gerku .i zu'aku le verba cu cadzu le bisli'''
:<code>The man bites the dog. [Left] the child walks-on the ice.</code>
:''The man bites the dog. Left of me, the child walks on the ice.''

In {{lex|example-random-id-MzxF}}, the origin point is the speaker, as is usual with {{jbo|zu'aku}}. {{lex|example-random-id-9Q0x}} makes the origin point of the tense the event described by the first sentence.

{{ind|general-imported|tense connected sentences|forethought mode}} Two sentences may also be connected in forethought by a tense relationship. Just like afterthought tense connection, forethought tense connection claims both sentences, and in addition claims that the time or space relationship specified by the tense holds between the events the two sentences describe.

{{ind|general-imported|imaginary journey|origin in tense forethought sentence connection}}  {{ind|general-imported|sentences|forethought tense connection of}}  {{ind|general-imported|forethought tense connection of sentences|order of}} The origin sentence is placed first, preceded by a tense plus {{vla|gi}}. Another {{vla|gi}} is used to separate the sentences:

{{dsp|example-random-id-9cXU}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-9cXU}}
{{judri|c10e16d6}}
:'''pugi mi klama le zarci gi mi klama le zdani'''
:<code>[past] I go-to the market [,] I go-to the house.</code>
:''Before I go to the market, I go to the house.''

A parallel construction can be used to express a tense relationship between sumti:

{{ind|general-imported|sumti|forethought tense connection of}}  {{ind|general-imported|imaginary journey|origin in tense forethought sumti connection}}  {{ind|general-imported|forethought tense connection of sumti|order of}}

{{dsp|example-random-id-o3Yg}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-o3Yg}}
{{judri|c10e16d7}}
:'''mi klama pugi le zarci gi le zdani'''
:<code>I go-to [past] the market [,] the house.</code>

Because English does not have any direct way of expressing a tense-like relationship between nouns, {{lex|example-random-id-o3Yg}} cannot be expressed in English without paraphrasing it either into {{lex|example-random-id-9cXU}} or else into “I go to the house before the market”, which is ambiguous &ndash; is the market going?

{{ind|general-imported|bridi-tails|forethought tense connection of}}  {{ind|general-imported|imaginary journey|origin in tense forethought bridi-tail connection}}  {{ind|general-imported|forethought tense connection of bridi-tails|order of}} Finally, a third forethought construction expresses a tense relationship between bridi-tails rather than whole bridi. (The construct known as a “bridi-tail” is explained fully in {{ls|section-compound-bridi}}; roughly speaking, it is a selbri, possibly with following sumti.) {{lex|example-random-id-vSCv}} is equivalent in meaning to {{lex|example-random-id-9cXU}} and {{lex|example-random-id-o3Yg}}:

{{dsp|example-random-id-vSCv}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-vSCv}}
{{judri|c10e16d8}}
:'''mi pugi klama le zarci gi klama le zdani'''
:<code>I [past] go-to the market [,] go-to the house.</code>
:''I, before going to the market, go to the house.''

{{ind|general-imported|tense connection of bridi-tails|meaning of}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense connection of sumti|meaning of}} In both {{lex|example-random-id-o3Yg}} and {{lex|example-random-id-vSCv}}, the underlying sentences 
:{{jbo|mi klama le zarci}} and 
:{{jbo|mi klama le zdani}} are not claimed; only the relationship in time between them is claimed.

{{ind|general-imported|tense afterthought connection forms|selma'o allowed}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense forethought connection forms|selma'o allowed}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense connection|expansions of}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense connection|equivalent meanings}} Both the forethought and the afterthought forms are appropriate with PU, ZI, FAhA, VA, and ZAhO tenses. In all cases, the equivalent forms are (where X and Y stand for sentences, and TENSE for a tense cmavo):



;'''subordinate:'''
:{{grammar|X TENSE le nu Y}}

;'''afterthought coordinate:'''
:{{grammar|Y .i+TENSE+bo X}}

;'''forethought coordinate:'''
:{{grammar|TENSE+gi X gi Y}}


{{ssp|section-tense-logical-connection}}
==Tensed logical connectives==
{{ind|general-imported|tensed logical connectives}}  {{ind|general-imported|logical connectives|tensed}} The Lojban tense system interacts with the Lojban logical connective system. That system is a separate topic, explained in 
{{lch|chapter-connectives}} and touched on only in summary here. By the rules of the logical connective system, {{lex|example-random-id-qehB}} through 17.3 are equivalent in meaning:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qehB}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qehB}}
{{judri|c10e17d1}}
:'''la teris. satre le mlatu .ije la teris. satre le ractu'''
:''Terry strokes the cat. And Terry strokes the rabbit.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEI1}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEI1}}
{{judri|c10e17d2}}
:'''la teris. satre le mlatu gi'e satre le ractu'''
:''Terry strokes the cat and strokes the rabbit.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEIm}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEIm}}
{{judri|c10e17d3}}
:'''la teris. satre le mlatu .e le ractu'''
:''Terry strokes the cat and the rabbit.''

Suppose we wish to add a tense relationship to the logical connective “and”? To say that Terry strokes the cat and later strokes the rabbit, we can combine a logical connective with a tense connective by placing the logical connective first, then the tense, and then the cmavo {{vla|bo}}, thus:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEiY}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEiY}}
{{judri|c10e17d4}}
{{ind|example|stroke cat then rabbit|example}}
{{ind|example|and then|example}}
:'''la teris. satre le mlatu .ijebabo la teris. satre le ractu'''
:''Terry strokes the cat. And then Terry strokes the rabbit.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEjn}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEjn}}
{{judri|c10e17d5}}
{{ind|example|stroke cat then rabbit|example}}
{{ind|example|and then|example}}
:'''la teris. satre le mlatu gi'ebabo satre le ractu'''
:''Terry strokes the cat, and then strokes the rabbit.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEKa}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEKa}}
{{judri|c10e17d6}}
{{ind|example|stroke cat then rabbit|example}}
{{ind|example|and then|example}}
:'''la teris. satre le mlatu .ebabo le ractu'''
:''Terry strokes the cat and then the rabbit.''

{{ind|general-imported|tensed logically connected sumti}}  {{ind|general-imported|tensed logically connected bridi-tails}}  {{ind|general-imported|tensed logically connected sentences}} {{lex|example-random-id-qEiY}} through 17.6 are equivalent in meaning. They are also analogous to {{lex|example-random-id-qehB}} through {{lex|example-random-id-qEIm}} respectively. The {{vla|bo}} is required for the same reason as in {{lex|example-random-id-9Q0x}}: to prevent the {{vla|ba}} from functioning as a sumti tcita for the following sumti (or, in {{lex|example-random-id-qEjn}}, from being attached to the following selbri).

{{ind|general-imported|tensed logical connectives|with tu'e…tu'u}}  {{ind|general-imported|tensed logical connectives|with ke…ke'e}} In addition to the {{vla|bo}} construction of {{lex|example-random-id-qEiY}} through {{lex|example-random-id-qEKa}}, there is also a form of tensed logical connective with 
{{vla|ke}}&hellip;{{vla|ke'e}} ( {{vla|tu'e}}&hellip;{{vla|tu'u}} for sentences). The logical connective system makes {{lex|example-random-id-qeL4}} through {{lex|example-random-id-qeLv}} equivalent in meaning:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qeL4}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qeL4}}
{{judri|c10e17d7}}
{{ind|example|carry sack and dog|example}}
:'''mi bevri le dakli .ije tu'e mi bevri le gerku .ija mi bevri le mlatu tu'u'''
:<code>I carry the sack. And (I carry the dog. And/or I carry the cat).</code>
:''I carry the sack. And I carry the dog, or I carry the cat, or I carry both.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qELN}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qELN}}
{{judri|c10e17d8}}
{{ind|example|carry sack and dog|example}}
:'''mi bevri le dakli gi'eke bevri le gerku gi'a bevri le mlatu'''
:<code>I carry the sack and (carry the dog and/or carry the cat).</code>
:''I carry the sack, and also carry the dog or carry the cat or carry both.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qeLv}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qeLv}}
{{judri|c10e17d9}}
{{ind|example|carry sack and dog|example}}
:'''mi bevri le dakli .eke le gerku .a le mlatu'''
:<code>I carry the sack and (the dog or the cat).</code>
:''I carry the sack and also the dog or the cat or both.''

Note the uniformity of the Lojban, as contrasted with the variety of ways in which the English provides for the correct grouping. In all cases, the meaning is that I carry the sack in any case, and either the cat or the dog or both.

To express that I carry the sack first (earlier in time), and then the dog or the cat or both simultaneously, I can insert tenses to form {{lex|example-random-id-qeLV}} through {{lex|example-random-id-qEnd}}:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qeLV}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qeLV}}
{{judri|c10e17d10}}
:'''mi bevri le dakli .ije ba tu'e mi bevri le gerku .ijacabo mi bevri le mlatu tu'u'''
:<code>I carry the sack. And [future] (I carry the dog. And/or [present] I carry the cat.)</code>
:''I carry the sack. And then I will carry the dog or I will carry the cat or I will carry both at once.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qeMo}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qeMo}}
{{judri|c10e17d11}}
:'''mi bevri le dakli gi'ebake bevri le gerku gi'acabo bevri le mlatu'''
:<code>I carry the sack and [future] (carry the dog and/or [present] carry the cat).</code>
:''I carry the sack and then will carry the dog or carry the cat or carry both at once.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEnd}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEnd}}
{{judri|c10e17d12}}
:'''mi bevri le dakli .ebake le gerku .acabo le mlatu'''
:<code>I carry the sack and [future] (the cat and/or [present] the dog).</code>
:''I carry the sack, and then the cat or the dog or both at once.''

{{ind|general-imported|tensed logically connected sumti|with grouping}}  {{ind|general-imported|tensed logically connected bridi-tails|with grouping}}  {{ind|general-imported|tensed logically connected sentences|with grouping}} {{lex|example-random-id-qeLV}} through {{lex|example-random-id-qEnd}} are equivalent in meaning to each other, and correspond to the tenseless {{lex|example-random-id-qeL4}} through {{lex|example-random-id-qeLv}} respectively.

{{ssp|section-tense-negation}}
==Tense negation==
{{ind|general-imported|ZAhO selma'o|contradictory negation of}}  {{ind|general-imported|FAhA selma'o|contradictory negation of}}  {{ind|general-imported|PU selma'o|contradictory negation of}}  {{ind|general-imported|negation|of tenses}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|negating}} Any bridi which involves tenses of selma'o PU, FAhA, or ZAhO can be contradicted by a 
:{{jbo|-nai}} suffixed to the tense cmavo. Some examples:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qXWF}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qXWF}}
{{judri|c10e18d1}}
:'''mi punai klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [past] [not] go-to the market.</code>
:''I didn't go to the market.''

{{ind|general-imported|negation of tenses|meaning of}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|contradictory negation of with nai}} As a contradictory negation, {{lex|example-random-id-qXWF}} implies that the bridi as a whole is false without saying anything about what is true. When the negated tense is a sumti tcita, 
:{{jbo|-nai}} negation indicates that the stated relationship does not hold:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEnq}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEnq}}
{{judri|c10e18d2}}
:'''mi klama le zarci canai le nu do klama le zdani'''
:<code>I go-to the market [present] [not] the event-of you go-to the house.</code>
:''It is not true that I went to the market at the same time that you went to the house.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qeNT}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qeNT}}
{{judri|c10e18d3}}
:'''le nanmu batci le gerku ne'inai le kumfa'''
:<code>The man bites the dog [within] [not] the room.</code>
:''The man didn't bite the dog inside the room.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEny}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEny}}
{{judri|c10e18d4}}
:'''mi morsi ca'onai le nu mi jmive'''
:<code>I am-dead [continuitive - negated] the event-of I live.</code>
:''It is false that I am dead during my life.''

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|NAhE selma'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense|contradictory negation contrasted with scalar negation of}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense|scalar negation contrasted with contradictory negation of}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense|scalar negation of with NAhE}} It is also possible to perform scalar negation of whole tense constructs by placing a member of NAhE before them. Unlike contradictory negation, scalar negation asserts a truth: that the bridi is true with some tense other than that specified. The following examples are scalar negation analogues of {{lex|example-random-id-qXWF}} to {{lex|example-random-id-qeNT}}:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEo1}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEo1}}
{{judri|c10e18d5}}
:'''mi na'e pu klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [non-] [past] go-to the market.</code>
:''I go to the market other than in the past.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEoN}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEoN}}
{{judri|c10e18d6}}
:'''le nanmu batci le gerku to'e ne'i le kumfa'''
:<code>The man bites the dog [opposite-of] [within] the room.</code>
:''The man bites the dog outside the room.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEqa}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEqa}}
{{judri|c10e18d7}}
:'''mi klama le zarci na'e ca le nu do klama le zdani'''
:<code>I go-to the market [non-] [present] the event-of you go-to the house.</code>
:''I went to the market at a time other than the time at which you went to the house.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qeQe}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qeQe}}
{{judri|c10e18d8}}
:'''mi morsi na'e ca'o le nu mi jmive'''
:<code>I am-dead [non-] [continuitive] the event-of I live.</code>
:''I am dead other than during my life.''

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|FAhA selma'o}}  {{ind|lojban-word-imported|PU selma'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|scalar negation of tenses|selma'o allowed with}}  {{ind|general-imported|contradictory negation of tenses|selma'o allowed with}} Unlike 
:{{jbo|-nai}} contradictory negation, scalar negation of tenses is not limited to PU and FAhA:

{{dsp|example-random-id-THJJ}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-THJJ}}
{{judri|c10e18d9}}
:'''le verba na'e ri'u cadzu le bisli'''
:<code>The child [non-] [right] walks-on the ice</code>
:''The child walks on the ice other than to my right.''

{{ind|general-imported|ROI selma'o|scalar negation of}}  {{ind|general-imported|TAhE selma'o|scalar negation of}} The use of 
:{{jbo|-nai}} on cmavo of TAhE and ROI has already been discussed in {{ls|section-interval-properties}}; this use is also a scalar negation.

{{ssp|section-caha}}
==Actuality, potentiality, capability: CAhA==
The following cmavo are discussed in this section:
<tab class=wikitable>
cmavo	selma'o	subclass	meaning
'''ca'a'''	CAhA	''actually is''
'''ka'e'''	CAhA	''is innately capable of''
'''nu'o'''	CAhA	''can but has not''
'''pu'i'''	CAhA	''can and has''
</tab>

{{ind|general-imported|innate capabilities|expressing implicitly}}  {{ind|general-imported|potential events|expressing implicitly}} Lojban bridi without tense markers may not necessarily refer to actual events: they may also refer to capabilities or potential events. For example:

{{dsp|example-random-id-HjjN}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-HjjN}}
{{judri|c10e19d1}}
{{ind|example|ducks swim|example}}
:'''ro datka cu flulimna'''
:<code>All ducks are-float-swimmers.</code>
:''All ducks swim by floating.''

{{ind|general-imported|actuality|Lojban contrasted with English in implying}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense|Lojban contrasted with English in implying actuality}} is a Lojban truth, even though the colloquial English translation is false or at best ambiguous. This is because the tenseless Lojban bridi doesn't necessarily claim that every duck is swimming or floating now or even at a specific time or place. Even if we add a tense marker to {{lex|example-random-id-HjjN}},

{{dsp|example-random-id-o9Yu}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-o9Yu}}
{{judri|c10e19d2}}
:'''ro datka ca flulimna'''
:<code>All ducks [present] are-float-swimmers.</code>
:''All ducks are now swimming by floating.''

the resulting {{lex|example-random-id-o9Yu}} might still be considered a truth, even though the colloquial English seems even more likely to be false. All ducks have the potential of swimming even if they are not exercising that potential at present. To get the full flavor of “All ducks are now swimming”, we must append a marker from selma'o CAhA to the tense, and say:

{{dsp|example-random-id-hXpB}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-hXpB}}
{{judri|c10e19d3}}
:'''ro datka ca ca'a flulimna'''
:<code>All ducks [present] [actual] are-float-swimmers.</code>
:''All ducks are now actually swimming by floating.''

{{ind|general-imported|sticky tenses|and CAhA}}  {{ind|general-imported|CAhA selma'o|making sticky}}  {{ind|general-imported|CAhA selma'o|order in tense construct}}  {{ind|general-imported|actual events|explicitly expressing}} A CAhA cmavo is always placed after any other tense cmavo, whether for time or for space. However, a CAhA cmavo comes before {{vla|ki}}, so that a CAhA condition can be made sticky.{{lex|example-random-id-hXpB}} is false in both Lojban and English, since it claims that the swimming is an actual, present fact, true of every duck that exists, whereas in fact there is at least one duck that is not swimming now.

{{ind|general-imported|innate capability|expressing explicitly}} Furthermore, some ducks are dead (and therefore sink); some ducks have just hatched (and do not know how to swim yet), and some ducks have been eaten by predators (and have ceased to exist as separate objects at all). Nevertheless, all these ducks have the innate capability of swimming &ndash; it is part of the nature of duckhood. The cmavo 
{{vla|ka'e}} expresses this notion of innate capability:

{{dsp|example-random-id-ApiH}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-ApiH}}
{{judri|c10e19d4}}
:'''ro datka ka'e flulimna'''
:<code>All ducks [capable] are-float-swimmers.</code>
:''All ducks are innately capable of swimming.''

{{ind|general-imported|innate properties|extension of from mass to individuals}} Under some epistemologies, innate capability can be extended in order to apply the innate properties of a mass to which certain individuals belong to the individuals themselves, even if those individuals are themselves not capable of fulfilling the claim of the bridi. For example:

{{dsp|example-random-id-ebcg}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-ebcg}}
{{judri|c10e19d5}}
{{ind|example|can see|example}}
:'''la djan. ka'e viska'''
:<code>John [capable] sees.</code>
:<code>John is innately capable of seeing.</code>
:''John can see.''

{{ind|general-imported|innate properties|extension to individuals not actually capable}} might be true about a human being named John, even though he has been blind since birth, because the ability to see is innately built into his nature as a human being. It is theoretically possible that conditions might occur that would enable John to see (a great medical discovery, for example). On the other hand,

{{dsp|example-random-id-NC6V}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-NC6V}}
{{judri|c10e19d6}}
:'''le cukta ka'e viska'''
:<code>The book [capable] sees.</code>
:''The book can see.''

is not true in most epistemologies, since the ability to see is not part of the innate nature of a book.

{{ind|general-imported|undemonstrated potential|expressing}} Consider once again the newly hatched ducks mentioned earlier. They have the potential of swimming, but have not yet demonstrated that potential. This may be expressed using {{vla|nu'o}}, the cmavo of CAhA for undemonstrated potential:

{{dsp|example-random-id-sHpR}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-sHpR}}
{{judri|c10e19d7}}
{{ind|example|infant ducks|example}}
:'''ro cifydatka nu'o flulimna'''
:<code>All infant-ducks [can but has not] are-float-swimmers.</code>
:<code>All infant ducks have an undemonstrated potential for swimming by floating.</code>

:''Baby ducks can swim but haven't yet.''

{{ind|general-imported|demonstrated potential|expressing}} Contrariwise, if Frank is not blind from birth, then {{vla|pu'i}} is appropriate:

{{dsp|example-random-id-VPfM}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-VPfM}}
{{judri|c10e19d8}}
:'''la frank. pu'i viska'''
:<code>Frank [can and has] sees.</code>
:<code>Frank has demonstrated a potential for seeing.</code>
:''Frank can see and has seen.''

{{ind|general-imported|actuality|expressing in past/future}}  {{ind|general-imported|potential|expressing in past/future}} Note that the glosses given at the beginning of this section for {{vla|ca'a}}, 
{{vla|nu'o}}, and 
{{vla|pu'i}} incorporate 
{{vla|ca}} into their meaning, and are really correct for 
:{{jbo|ca ca'a}}, 

:{{jbo|ca nu'o}}, and 

:{{jbo|ca pu'i}}. However, the CAhA cmavo are perfectly meaningful with other tenses than the present:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qER7}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qER7}}
{{judri|c10e19d9}}
:'''mi pu ca'a klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [past] [actual] go-to the store.</code>
:''I actually went to the store.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qera}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qera}}
{{judri|c10e19d10}}
:'''la frank. ba nu'o klama le zdani'''
:<code>Frank [future] [can but has not] goes-to the store.</code>
:<code>Frank could have, but will not have, gone to the store</code>
:''(at some understood moment in the future).''

{{ind|general-imported|tenses with elided CAhA|meaning}} As always in Lojban tenses, a missing CAhA can have an indeterminate meaning, or the context can be enough to disambiguate it. Saying

{{dsp|example-random-id-IKGW}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-IKGW}}
{{judri|c10e19d11}}
{{ind|example|inflammable|example}}
:'''ta jelca'''
:<code>That burns/is-burning/might-burn/will-burn.</code>

with no CAhA specified can translate the two very different English sentences “That is on fire” and “That is inflammable.” The first demands immediate action (usually), whereas the second merely demands caution. The two cases can be disambiguated with:

{{dsp|example-random-id-5tur}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-5tur}}
{{judri|c10e19d12}}
:'''ta ca ca'a jelca'''
:<code>That [present] [actual] burns.</code>
:''That is on fire.''

and

{{dsp|example-random-id-PRrR}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-PRrR}}
{{judri|c10e19d13}}
:'''ta ka'e jelca'''
:<code>That [capable] burns.</code>
:<code>That is capable of burning.</code>
:''That is inflammable.''

{{ind|general-imported|observative with elided CAhA|convention}} When no indication is given, as in the simple observative

{{dsp|example-random-id-FWoz}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-FWoz}}
{{judri|c10e19d14}}
:'''jelca'''
:''It burns!''

the prudent Lojbanist will assume the meaning “Fire!”

{{ssp|section-connected-tenses}}
==Logical and non-logical connections between tenses==
Like many things in Lojban, tenses may be logically connected; logical connection is explained in more detail in {{lch|chapter-connectives}}. Some of the terminology in this section will be clear only if you already understand logical connectives.

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|JA selma'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|logically connected tenses|expansion to sentences}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|logically connected with JA}}  {{ind|general-imported|logically connected tenses|with JA}} The appropriate logical connectives belong to selma'o JA. A logical connective between tenses can always be expanded to one between sentences:

{{dsp|example-random-id-XAj7}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-XAj7}}
{{judri|c10e20d1}}
:'''mi pu je ba klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [past] and [future] go-to the market.</code>
:''I went and will go to the market.''

means the same as:

{{dsp|example-random-id-BWI5}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-BWI5}}
{{judri|c10e20d2}}
:'''mi pu klama le zarci .ije mi ba klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [past] go-to the market. And I [future] go-to the market.</code>
:''I went to the market, and I will go to the market.''

{{ind|general-imported|tenses|connected|with negation}} Tense connection and tense negation are combined in:

{{dsp|example-random-id-Tuz1}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Tuz1}}
{{judri|c10e20d3}}
:'''mi punai je canai je ba klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [past] [not] and [present] [not] and [future] go-to the market.</code>
:''I haven't yet gone to the market, but I will in future.''
{{lex|example-random-id-Tuz1}} is far more specific than

{{dsp|example-random-id-J5jJ}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-J5jJ}}
{{judri|c10e20d4}}
:'''mi ba klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [future] go-to the market.</code>

which only says that I will go, without claiming anything about my past or present. {{vla|ba}} does not imply 
:{{jbo|punai}} or 
:{{jbo|canai}}; to compel that interpretation, either a logical connection or a ZAhO is needed.

{{ind|general-imported|connected tenses|negation of compared with negation in connective}} Tense negation can often be removed in favor of negation in the logical connective itself. The following examples are equivalent in meaning:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qErC}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qErC}}
{{judri|c10e20d5}}
:'''mi mo'izu'anai je mo'iri'u cadzu'''
:<code>I [motion] [left-not] and [motion] [right] walk.</code>
:''I walk not leftward but rightward.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qeRL}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qeRL}}
{{judri|c10e20d6}}
:'''mi mo'izu'a naje mo'iri'u cadzu'''
:<code>I [motion] [left] not-and [motion] [right] walk.</code>
:''I walk not leftward but rightward.''

{{ind|general-imported|tenses|possible groupings of}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|forethought logical connections}} There are no forethought logical connections between tenses allowed by the grammar, to keep tenses simpler. Nor is there any way to override simple left-grouping of the connectives, the Lojban default.

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|GAhO selma'o}}  {{ind|lojban-word-imported|JOI selma'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|intervals|expressing by endpoints with bi'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|non-logical connection of}} The non-logical connectives of selma'o JOI, BIhI, and GAhO are also permitted between tenses. One application is to specify intervals not by size, but by their end-points ( {{vla|bi'o}} belongs to selma'o BIhI, and connects the end-points of an ordered interval, like English “from ... to”):

{{dsp|example-random-id-KQUM}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-KQUM}}
{{judri|c10e20d7}}
:'''mi puza bi'o bazu vasxu'''
:<code>I [past] [medium] from ... to [future] [long] breathe.</code>
:''I breathe from a medium time ago till a long time to come.''

(It is to be hoped that I have a long life ahead of me.)

One additional use of non-logical connectives within tenses is discussed in {{ls|section-sub-events}}. Other uses will probably be identified in future.

{{ssp|section-sub-events}}
==Sub-events==

{{ind|general-imported|tenses|non-logical connection of for sub-events}} Another application of non-logical tense connection is to talk about sub-events of events. Consider a six-shooter: a gun which can fire six bullets in succession before reloading. If I fire off the entire magazine twice, I can express the fact in Lojban thus:

{{dsp|example-random-id-9CqG}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-9CqG}}
{{judri|c10e21d1}}
{{ind|example|six-shooter|example}}
{{ind|example|on two occasions|example}}
:'''mi reroi pi'u xaroi cecla le seldanti'''
:<code>I [twice] [cross-product] [six times] shoot the projectile-launcher.</code>
:''On two occasions, I fire the gun six times.''

{{ind|general-imported|cross product|with tenses}}  {{ind|general-imported|Cartesian product|with tenses}}  {{ind|general-imported|pi'u|use in connecting tenses}} It would be confusing, though grammatical, to run the {{vla|reroi}} and the 
:{{jbo|xaroi}} directly together. However, the non-logical connective {{vla|pi'u}} expresses a Cartesian product (also known as a cross product) of two sets. In this case, there is a set of two firings each of which is represented by a set of six shots, for twelve shots in all (hence the name “product”: the product of 2 and 6 is 12). Its use specifies very precisely what occurs.

{{ind|general-imported|event contours|strings of}}  {{ind|general-imported|interval properties|strings of}} In fact, you can specify strings of interval properties and event contours within a single tense without the use of a logical or non-logical connective cmavo. This allows tenses of the type:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qES9}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qES9}}
{{judri|c10e21d2}}
:'''la djordj. ca'o co'a ciska'''
:<code>George [continuitive] [initiative] writes.</code>
:''George continues to start to write.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qetE}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qetE}}
{{judri|c10e21d3}}
:'''mi reroi ca'o xaroi darxi le damri'''
:<code>I [twice] [continuitive] [six times] hit the drum.</code>
:''On two occasions, I continue to beat the drum six times.''

{{ssp|section-jai}}
==Conversion of sumti tcita: JAI==
The following cmavo are discussed in this section:
<tab class=wikitable>
cmavo	selma'o	subclass	meaning
'''jai'''	JAI	''tense conversion''
'''fai'''	FA	''indefinite place''
</tab>

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|SE selma'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|conversion|definition}} Conversion is the regular Lojban process of moving around the places of a place structure. The cmavo of selma'o SE serve this purpose, exchanging the first place with one of the others:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEu5}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEu5}}
{{judri|c10e22d1}}
:'''mi cu klama le zarci'''
:<code>I go-to the market.</code>

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEu9}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEu9}}
{{judri|c10e22d2}}
:'''le zarci cu se klama mi'''
:<code>The market is-gone-to by-me.</code>

{{ind|general-imported|jai with tense|as equivalent of SE in grammar}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense conversion|accessing tense of bridi with jai}}  {{ind|general-imported|conversion|accessing tense of bridi with jai}} It is also possible to bring a place that is specified by a sumti tcita (for the purposes of this chapter, a tense sumti tcita) to the front, by using {{vla|jai}} plus the tense as the grammatical equivalent of SE:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEvD}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEvD}}
{{judri|c10e22d3}}
{{ind|example|rat eats cheese in park|example}}
:'''le ratcu cu citka le cirla vi le panka'''
:<code>The rat eats the cheese [short distance] the park.</code>
:''The rat eats the cheese in the park.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEWB}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEWB}}
{{judri|c10e22d4}}
{{ind|example|rat eats cheese in park|example}}
:'''le panka cu jai vi citka le cirla fai le ratcu'''
:<code>The park is-the-place-of eating the cheese by-the rat.</code>
:''The park is where the rat eats the cheese.''

{{ind|general-imported|tense conversion|accessing original first place with fai}} In {{lex|example-random-id-qEWB}}, the construction JAI+tense converts the location sumti into the first place. The previous first place has nowhere to go, since the location sumti is not a numbered place; however, it can be inserted back into the bridi with {{vla|fai}}, the indefinite member of selma'o FA.

(The other members of FA are used to mark the first, second, etc. places of a bridi explicitly:

{{dsp|example-random-id-YS3i}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-YS3i}}
{{judri|c10e22d5}}
:'''fa mi cu klama fe le zarci'''

means the same as

{{dsp|example-random-id-4DGL}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-4DGL}}
{{judri|c10e22d6}}
:'''fe le zarci cu klama fa mi'''

as well as the simple

{{dsp|example-random-id-Q6J9}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Q6J9}}
{{judri|c10e22d7}}
:'''mi cu klama le zarci'''

in which the place structure is determined by position.)

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|LE selma'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense conversion|use in sumti descriptions}} Like SE conversion, JAI+tense conversion is especially useful in descriptions with LE selma'o:

{{dsp|example-random-id-esDa}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-esDa}}
{{judri|c10e22d8}}
{{ind|example|place of eating|example}}
:'''mi viska le jai vi citka be le cirla'''
:<code>I saw the place-of eating the cheese.</code>

Here the eater of the cheese is elided, so no {{vla|fai}} appears.

{{ind|general-imported|tense conversion|of temporal tenses}} Of course, temporal tenses are also usable with JAI:

{{dsp|example-random-id-nSnh}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-nSnh}}
{{judri|c10e22d9}}
:'''mi djuno fi le jai ca morsi be fai la djan.'''
<code>I know about the [present] is-dead of-the-one-called “John”.</code>
:<code>I know the time of John's death.</code>
:''I know when John died.''

{{ssp|section-tenses-vs-modals}}
==Tenses versus modals==
{{ind|general-imported|modals|contrasted with tenses in semantics}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|contrasted with modals in semantics}}  {{ind|general-imported|modals|compared with tenses in syntax}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|compared with modals in syntax}} Grammatically, every use of tenses seen so far is exactly paralleled by some use of modals as explained in {{lch|chapter-sumti-tcita}}. Modals and tenses alike can be followed by sumti, can appear before the selbri, can be used in pure and mixed connections, can participate in JAI conversions. The parallelism is perfect. However, there is a deep difference in the semantics of tense constructs and modal constructs, grounded in historical differences between the two forms. Originally, modals and tenses were utterly different things in earlier versions of Loglan; only in Lojban have they become grammatically interchangeable. And even now, differences in semantics continue to be maintained.

{{ind|general-imported|modals|importance of 1st sumti place for sumti tcita use}} The core distinction is that whereas the modal bridi

{{dsp|example-random-id-YLmV}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-YLmV}}
{{judri|c10e23d1}}
:'''mi nelci do mu'i le nu do nelci mi'''
:<code>I like you with-motivation the event-of you like me.</code>
:''I like you because you like me.''

places the 
:{{jbo|le nu}} sumti in the x1 place of the gismu {{vla|mukti}} (which underlies the modal {{vla|mu'i}}), namely the motivating event, the tensed bridi

{{dsp|example-random-id-zXi8}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-zXi8}}
{{judri|c10e23d2}}
:'''mi nelci do ba le nu do nelci mi'''
:<code>I like you after the event-of you like me.</code>
:''I like you after you like me.''

{{ind|general-imported|tenses|importance of 2nd sumti place for sumti tcita use}} places the 
:{{jbo|le nu}} sumti in the x2 place of the gismu {{vla|balvi}} (which underlies the tense {{vla|ba}}), namely the point of reference for the future tense. Paraphrases of {{lex|example-random-id-YLmV}} and {{lex|example-random-id-zXi8}}, employing the brivla {{vla|mukti}} and {{vla|balvi}} explicitly, would be:

{{dsp|example-random-id-JbEU}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-JbEU}}
{{judri|c10e23d3}}
:'''le nu do nelci mi cu mukti le nu mi nelci do'''
:<code>The event-of you like me motivates the event-of I like you.</code>
:''Your liking me is the motive for my liking you.''

and

{{dsp|example-random-id-8sjA}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-8sjA}}
{{judri|c10e23d4}}
:'''le nu mi nelci do cu balvi le nu do nelci mi'''
:<code>The event-of I like you is after the event of you like me.</code>
:''My liking you follows (in time) your liking me.''

(Note that the paraphrase is not perfect due to the difference in what is claimed; {{lex|example-random-id-JbEU}} and {{lex|example-random-id-8sjA}} claim only the causal and temporal relationships between the events, not the existence of the events themselves.)

{{ind|general-imported|afterthought sentence connection|modal contrasted with tense}} As a result, the afterthought sentence-connective forms of {{lex|example-random-id-YLmV}} and {{lex|example-random-id-zXi8}} are, respectively:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qewe}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qewe}}
{{judri|c10e23d5}}
:'''mi nelci do .imu'ibo do nelci mi'''
:<code>I like you. [That is] Because you like me.</code>

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEWp}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEWp}}
{{judri|c10e23d6}}
:'''do nelci mi .ibabo mi nelci do'''
:''You like me. Afterward, I like you.''

In {{lex|example-random-id-qewe}}, the order of the two bridi 
:{{jbo|mi nelci do}} and 
:{{jbo|do nelci mi}} is the same as in {{lex|example-random-id-YLmV}}. In {{lex|example-random-id-qEWp}}, however, the order is reversed: the origin point 
:{{jbo|do nelci mi}} physically appears before the future-time event 
:{{jbo|mi nelci do}}. In both cases, the bridi characterizing the event in the x2 place appears before the bridi characterizing the event in the x1 place of {{vla|mukti}} or {{vla|balvi}}.

{{ind|general-imported|afterthought tense connection|contrasted with forethought in likeness to modal connection}}  {{ind|general-imported|forethought tense connection|contrasted with afterthought in likeness to modal connection}}  {{ind|general-imported|forethought connections|modal compared with tense in semantics}} In forethought connections, however, the asymmetry between modals and tenses is not found. The forethought equivalents of {{lex|example-random-id-qewe}} and {{lex|example-random-id-qEWp}} are

{{dsp|example-random-id-ENKj}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-ENKj}}
{{judri|c10e23d7}}
:'''mu'igi do nelci mi gi mi nelci do'''
:''Because you like me, I like you.''

and

{{dsp|example-random-id-r7KK}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-r7KK}}
{{judri|c10e23d8}}
:'''bagi do nelci mi gi mi nelci do'''
:''After you like me, I like you.''

respectively.

{{ind|general-imported|modal sentence connection|table of equivalent schemata}} The following modal sentence schemata (where X and Y represent sentences) all have the same meaning:


:'''{{grammar|X .i BAI bo Y}}'''
:'''{{grammar|BAI gi Y gi X}}'''
:'''{{grammar|X BAI le nu Y}}'''
{{ind|general-imported|tense sentence connection|table of equivalent schemata}} whereas the following tensed sentence schemata also have the same meaning:

:'''{{grammar|X .i TENSE bo Y}}'''
:'''{{grammar|TENSE gi X gi Y}}'''
:'''{{grammar|Y TENSE le nu X}}'''
neglecting the question of what is claimed. In the modal sentence schemata, the modal tag is always followed by Y, the sentence representing the event in the x1 place of the gismu that underlies the BAI. In the tensed sentences, no such simple rule exists.

{{ssp|section-tense-questions}}
==Tense questions: {{vla|cu'e}}==
The following cmavo is discussed in this section:
<tab class=wikitable>
cmavo	selma'o	subclass	meaning
'''cu'e'''	CUhE	''tense question''
</tab>

{{ind|general-imported|ma|for tense questions}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense questions with ma}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense questions|methods of asking}} There are two main ways to ask questions about tense. The main English tense question words are “When?” and “Where?”. These may be paraphrased respectively as “At what time?” and “At what place?” In these forms, their Lojban equivalents simply involve a tense plus {{vla|ma}}, the Lojban sumti question:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEwW}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEwW}}
{{judri|c10e24d1}}
{{ind|example|when|example}}
:'''do klama le zdani ca ma'''
:<code>You go-to the house [present] [what sumti?].</code>
:<code>You go to the house at what time?</code>
:''When do you go to the house?''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEX2}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEX2}}
{{judri|c10e24d2}}
{{ind|example|where|example}}
:'''le verba vi ma pu cadzu le bisli'''
:<code>The child [short space] [what sumti?] [past] walks-on the ice.</code>
:<code>The child at/near what place walked on the ice?</code>
:''Where did the child walk on the ice?''

{{ind|general-imported|modal-or-tense question|with cu'e}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense-or-modal questions|with cu'e}} There is also a non-specific tense and modal question, {{vla|cu'e}}, belonging to selma'o CUhE. This can be used wherever a tense or modal construct can be used.

{{dsp|example-random-id-4dAJ}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-4dAJ}}
{{judri|c10e24d3}}
{{ind|example|when/where/how|example}}
:'''le nanmu cu'e batci le gerku'''
:<code>The man [what tense?] bites the dog.</code>
:''When/Where/How does the man bite the dog?''

{{ind|general-imported|answers|to tense-or-modal questions}} Possible answers to {{lex|example-random-id-4dAJ}} might be:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qeya}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qeya}}
{{judri|c10e24d4}}
:'''va'''
:<code>[medium space].</code>
:''Some ways from here.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEYe}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEYe}}
{{judri|c10e24d5}}
:'''puzu'''
:<code>[past] [long time].</code>
:''A long time ago.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEyQ}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEyQ}}
{{judri|c10e24d6}}
:'''vi le lunra'''
:<code>[short space] The moon.</code>
:''On the moon.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qez6}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qez6}}
{{judri|c10e24d7}}
:'''pu'o'''
:<code>[inchoative]</code>
:''He hasn't yet done so.''

or even the modal reply (from selma'o BAI; See {{ls|section-BAI}}):

{{dsp|example-random-id-Vqgy}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Vqgy}}
{{judri|c10e24d8}}
:'''seka'a le briju'''
:<code>With-destination the office.</code>

{{ind|general-imported|modal-or-tense questions|pre-specifying some information}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense-or-modal questions|pre-specifying some information}}  {{ind|general-imported|cu'e|combining with other tense cmavo}} The only way to combine {{vla|cu'e}} with other tense cmavo is through logical connection, which makes a question that pre-specifies some information:

{{dsp|example-random-id-QTts}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-QTts}}
{{judri|c10e24d9}}
{{ind|example|when else|example}}
{{ind|example|sowed grain|example}}
:'''do puzi je cu'e sombo le gurni'''
:<code>You [past] [short] and [when?] sow the grain?</code>
:''You sowed the grain a little while ago; when else do you sow it?''

Additionally, the logical connective itself can be replaced by a question word:

{{ind|general-imported|tense questions|by using logical connective question}}

{{dsp|example-random-id-I6xI}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-I6xI}}
{{judri|c10e24d10}}
:'''la .artr. pu je'i ba nolraitru'''
:<code>Arthur [past] [which?] [future] is-a-king</code>
:''Was Arthur a king or will he be?''

Answers to {{lex|example-random-id-I6xI}} would be logical connectives such as {{vla|je}}, meaning “both”, 
:{{jbo|naje}} meaning “the latter”, or {{vla|jenai}} meaning “the former”.

{{ssp|section-explicit-magnitudes}}
==Explicit magnitudes==
It is a limitation of the VA and ZI system of specifying magnitudes that they can only prescribe vague magnitudes: small, medium, or large. In order to express both an origin point and an exact distance, the Lojban construction called a “termset” is employed. (Termsets are explained further in {{ls|section-termsets}} and {{ls|section-quantifier-grouping}}.) It is grammatical for a termset to be placed after a tense or modal tag rather than a sumti, which allows both the origin of the imaginary journey and its distance to be specified. Here is an example:

{{dsp|example-random-id-7Lys}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-7Lys}}
{{judri|c10e25d1}}
:'''la frank. sanli zu'a nu'i la djordj. la'u lo mitre be li mu [nu'u]'''
:<code>Frank stands [left] [start termset] George [quantity] a thing-measuring-in-meters the-number 5 [end termset].</code>
:''Frank is standing five meters to the left of George.''

Here the termset extends from the {{vla|nu'i}} to the implicit {{vla|nu'u}} at the end of the sentence, and includes the terms 
:{{jbo|la djordj.}}, which is the unmarked origin point, and the tagged sumti 
:{{jbo|lo mitre be li mu}}, which the cmavo {{vla|la'u}} (of selma'o BAI, and meaning “with quantity”; See {{ls|section-BAI}}) marks as a quantity. Both terms are governed by the tag {{vla|zu'a}}
It is not necessary to have both an origin point and an explicit magnitude: a termset may have only a single term in it. A less precise version of {{lex|example-random-id-7Lys}} is:

{{dsp|example-random-id-RWEE}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-RWEE}}
{{judri|c10e25d2}}
:'''la frank. sanli zu'a nu'i la'u lo mitre be li mu'''
:<code>Frank stands [left] [termset] [quantity] a thing-measuring-in-meters the-number 5.</code>
:''Frank stands five meters to the left.''

{{ssp|section-exercise}}
==Finally (an exercise for the much-tried reader)==

{{dsp|example-random-id-NxGB}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-NxGB}}
{{judri|c10e26d1}}
:'''.a'o do pu seju ba roroi ca'o fe'e su'oroi jimpe fi le lojbo temci selsku ciste'''

{{ssp|section-tense-selmaho-summary}}
==Summary of tense selma'o==
{{ind|general-imported|tense selma'o|summary of}}
<tab class=wikitable>
cmavo	selma'o	subclass	meaning
'''PU'''	temporal direction''
 pu = past, ca = present, ba = future''

'''ZI'''	temporal distance''
 zi = short, za = medium, zu = long''

'''ZEhA'''	temporal interval''
 ze'i = short, ze'a = medium, ze'u = long, ze'e = infinite''

'''ROI'''	objective quantified tense flag''
 noroi = never, paroi = once, ..., roroi = always, etc.''
 pare'u = the first time, rere'u = the second time, etc.''

'''TAhE'''	subjective quantified tense''
 di'i = regularly, na'o = typically, ru'i = continuously, ta'e = habitually''

'''ZAhO'''	event contours''
 see Section 10''

'''FAhA'''	spatial direction''
 see Section 28''

'''VA'''	spatial distance''
 vi = short, va = medium, vu = long''

'''VEhA'''	spatial interval''
 ve'i = short, ve'a = medium, ve'u = long, ve'e = infinite''

'''VIhA'''	spatial dimensionality''
 vi'i = line, vi'a = plane, vi'u = space, vi'e = space-time''

'''FEhE'''	spatial interval modifier flag''
 fe'enoroi = nowhere, fe'eroroi = everywhere, fe'eba'o = beyond, etc.''

'''MOhI'''	spatial movement flag''
 mo'i = motion; see Section 28''

'''KI'''	set or reset sticky tense''
 tense+“ki” = set, “ki” alone = reset''

'''CUhE'''	tense question, reference point''
 cu'e = asks for a tense or aspect, nau = use speaker’s reference point''

'''JAI'''	tense conversion''
 jaica = the time of, jaivi = the place of, etc.''
</tab>
